 2           1.      This case concerns spyware. Granola designed and created an AI notetaking product

 4 virtual meetings without their knowledge or consent.

 5           2.      Granola intentionally designed this software so that it need not be disclosed to those

 6 participating in virtual meetings. This is contrary to a majority of AI notetaking products on the

 7 market, where the AI notetaking software is made known before or at the start of the virtual meeting,

 8 many with the option to “boot” or “kick out” AI notetakers.
 9           3.      Unlike its competitors, Granola purposefully created and designed its technology to
10 do the opposite. Granola boasts that “[o]ther people in the room won’t know” Granola’s technology

11 is intercepting, recording, processing, and using their communications as the “distinction that

12 matters most” between Granola and other AI notetaking apps.1

13           4.      Worse, Granola does not merely passively record unknowing participants—a

14 quintessential wiretap—but also, by default, uses the contents of those communications for its own

15 commercial purposes, including training its AI systems. This setting can only be turned off by

16 Granola users, which excludes individuals like Plaintiff and Class Members who did not authorize

17 or consent to Granola’s secret recording practices in the first place.

18           5.      Plaintiff and the Class are participants in conversations that were intercepted,

19 recorded, transcribed in real time, and exploited by Granola, without their knowledge or consent.

20 This conduct constitutes an extreme invasion of Plaintiff’s and Class Members’ privacy. It also

21 violates each of the laws described herein.

22           6.      Given the secret and undisclosed nature of Defendants’ conduct, additional

23 evidence supporting Plaintiff’s claims, including the full extent of the sensitive personal information

24 Defendants intercepted and how they used that information, will be revealed in discovery.

 1          B.     How Granola AI’s Notetaking Feature Works

 2          48.    To create meeting notes, Granola uses the computer’s “system audio and

 3 microphone” to capture and transcribe the participants’ communications.24 When the Granola user

 4 speaks, Granola captures the communication through the computer’s microphone input. When other

 5 meeting participants speak, Granola captures their communications through the computer’s system-

 6 audio output.

 7          49.    Because Granola “uses [the] system audio to capture transcription,” it “captur[es]

 8 whatever audio inputs and outputs happen on [the] computer,” and “can transcribe any call where
 9 the audio plays through your computer—including calls from VoIP or internet calling apps.”25

10          50.    Granola’s technology “passes [the] audio directly from your microphone and system

11 audio” to its transcription vendor—who acts at Granola’s direction and as its agent—for the express

12 purpose of creating the AI transcription.26

13          51.    This acquisition, transmission, and processing occurs contemporaneously with the

14 underlying communications. As the participants speak, Granola captures their “live”

15 communications and uses the intercepted communication to generate and display a real-time

16 transcript while the meeting is still taking place and before the communications have come to rest.27

17          52.    Indeed, Granola’s own description confirms that it does not obtain the

18 communications from storage after they have come to rest. Granola expressly states that it “does not

19 record or save audio or video at any point during the call[.]”28 Nor does it allow transcription of

20 previously recorded audio files. Instead, it “passes audio directly from your microphone and system

21 audio” and uses that audio to generate a “live transcript” during the ongoing meeting.29 Thus, by

22 Granola’s own account, it acquires and processes the communications in real time as they are being

23 transmitted and received—not later from a stored recording.
